newsitem.title: USA: Minn. groups urge Fed's Stern not to raise rates.
newsitem.headline: Minn. groups urge Fed's Stern not to raise rates.

text.p: Representatives of several Minneapolis-area citizens and labor groups on Thursday urged Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Gary Stern to refrain from raising interest rates.
"Real short- and long-term interest rates are already high by historical standards," they said in a letter to Stern.

"A further monetary tightening would take the familiar toll on working families' jobs and purchasing power. Higher rates also would exacerbate mortgage and credit card delinquencies, which have already reached levels unseen in many years," the letter said.
The letter was signed by representatives of groups such as the Jobs Now coalition, the Minnesota Council of Churches, the Minnesota Citizens for Tax Justice, and several labor groups.

The Fed's next policy-making meeting is on Sept 24. At the last Fed meeting in July, Stern was the sole dissenter from the majority of central bank policy makers. He supported a short-term interest rate rise, while the other members voted to keep rates steady.
The letter also raised concern about a recent study by the General Accounting Office, a congressional watchdog agency, which criticized the Fed's management and spending practices.

A spokeswoman for the Minneapolis Fed confirmed that Stern had received the letter. She said he was not immediately available for comment, citing the Fed's "blackout" period in which officials generally do not comment on monetary policy within the week prior to a meeting.
